Hi Olivia — appreciate the clarity. Attaching a first-pass MAP that maps acceptance gates to documents, owners, and suggested due dates. High-level notes: 

- We recommend the following sequence: (A) complete procurement commercial terms and sign order form; (B) signature on MSA that covers service-level obligations; (C) DPA execution in parallel with evidence handoff (if HelixCare requires HSM/KMS details sooner we can push DPA earlier).
- Redlines to the MSA tend to drive the longest legal loop; if your legal team can triage non-essential redlines (audit frequency, data residency), we can parallelize onboarding activities.
- I’ve assigned Redwood owners for each evidence item; please confirm HelixCare assigned owners in the MAP.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the MAP and align owners tomorrow afternoon — looping in Karthik and Laura for procurement/legal sequencing.

Subject: Re: Pilot sequencing questions — ownership on legal/evidence windows

Thanks, Maya. A couple of procurement-level clarifications from Redwood’s side so HelixCare can finalize the internal schedule: 

1) Order form vs MSA: Is HelixCare comfortable signing the order form (pricing/term-length) prior to MSA signature, provided the order form references the MSA as the governing agreement? If yes, we can treat the order form as the initial commitment and run MSA parallel review. If no, the MSA needs to be prioritized first.

2) DPA timing: For pilots that don't handle PHI, we can execute a standard DPA template quickly. If HelixCare needs extra controls (on-prem ingestion, HSM), we will need to surface that early because it affects environment setup.

3) Evidence staging: we can accept a staggered evidence delivery — lowest friction items (SOC 2 report URL, contact for audit) should be provided before onboarding starts. Anything requiring internal engineering work (KMS proof, private VPC checks) must be flagged with an estimated engineering lead time.

I’ll join the sync. Laura — can you confirm whether Redwood’s legal team can provide a redline with tracked problem areas by end of week if HelixCare confirms order-form-first?

Karthik
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

- Jan 22: HelixCare to confirm whether order form may be signed as conditional commitment. (Owner: Olivia B.)
- Jan 25: Redwood to issue tracked redline to MSA (Owner: Laura B.)
- Jan 28: HelixCare legal to return a prioritized list of absolute blockers (Owner: Samuel R.)
- Feb 02: Final commercial signoff on order form (Owner: Procurement Team)
- Feb 06: DPA execution (target; Owner: HelixCare legal + Redwood legal)

- Order form-first conditional path accepted by HelixCare; any MSA items that will take more than 30 days to resolve must be surfaced and accepted as exceptions.
- Evidence staging: HelixCare will provide SOC 2 URL and audit contact by Jan 26; KMS/HSM details by Feb 02 if required.
- Escalation path: if any gating item is identified as high-risk, Redwood will open a parallel technical exception review with Marcus Lin (cc’d).

Attachments: HelixCare_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated with owners and dates), MSA_redline_draft.pdf
